profile.reading: Per the English Wikipedia article on the Terminal Commerce Building, this Philadelphia facility sits at 401 North Broad Street in the Callowhill neighborhood and totals over 1.3 million square feet (528 by 225 feet). Built 1929 to 1931 by the Reading Company as a combined office, showroom, parking garage, warehouse, and freight station, it is a fourteen story Art Deco front section with a twelve story H shaped rear warehouse, added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1996. Netrality Properties acquired the building in March 2014 and operates it as one of the largest interconnection and colocation facilities on the East Coast, described as the most fiber dense, network neutral facility between New York and Virginia.

reading.body:
Terminal Commerce Building is an Art Deco warehouse and office tower in Philadelphia's Callowhill neighborhood that Netrality Properties has operated as a colocation facility since 2014. The building totals over 1.3 million square feet across fourteen stories of office and showroom space fronting a twelve-story rear warehouse. Published power specifications for this facility are not available, so its capacity relative to AI infrastructure cannot be assessed from operator disclosures.

Among the fourteen mapped data center facilities in Pennsylvania, only four publish power capacity figures totaling 22.2 megawatts. This campus ranks fifth by published megawatts in the state, meaning its disclosed capacity falls below the published threshold used to rank the state's facilities. Pennsylvania's published capacity remains sparse compared to the facility count, indicating most operators in the state do not disclose power specifications.

The facility's identity as a network-neutral colocation site with high fiber density between New York and Virginia positions it in the interconnection market rather than hyperscale compute. Without published power, cooling, or IT load specifications, Terminal Commerce Building cannot be evaluated for AI workload suitability or contribution to regional AI scaling capacity.
